attributes.transcription: \v 5 In the time of Herod king of Judea there was a priest named Zechariah, who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah; his wife Elizabeth was also a descendant of Aaron. \v 6 Both of them were righteous in the sight of God, observing all the Lord’s commands and decrees blamelessly. \v 7 But they were childless because Elizabeth was not able to conceive, and they were both very old.

\v 21 Meanwhile, the people were waiting for Zechariah and wondering why he stayed so long in the temple. \v 22 When he came out, he could not speak to them. They realized he had seen a vision in the temple, for he kept making signs to them but remained unable to speak.

\v 23 When his time of service was completed, he returned home. \v 24 After this his wife Elizabeth became pregnant and for five months remained in seclusion. \v 25 “The Lord has done this for me,” she said. “In these days he has shown his favor and taken away my disgrace among the people.”

Below is an explanation of who Luke was, drawing from our resources:
Luke’s Background and Identity

Gentile Physician:Luke was not only a devoted follower of Christ but also a trained physician. His title, "the beloved doctor," indicates both his medical expertise and the special bond he shared with the apostle Paul.

Companion of Paul:Luke joined Paul on several of his missionary journeys. He was present during significant moments, including Paul's challenges, imprisonments, and journeys, reflecting his loyalty and willingness to support the ministry despite hardships.

Author of Two New Testament Books:Luke is credited with writing both the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles. His writings make up roughly one-quarter of the New Testament. 

Gospel of Luke: Presents a detailed, historically-informed account of Jesus’ life, emphasizing themes of joy, prayer, and the work of the Holy Spirit. Luke wrote this Gospel for a primarily Gentile audience, highlighting that salvation through Jesus Christ extends to all peoples, both Jews and Gentiles. 
Acts of the Apostles: Continues the narrative following Jesus’ ascension by detailing the early Church’s growth, the spread of the Gospel, and the challenges faced by the first believers.


Focus on Compassion and Healing:His background as a physician is evident in the way he records many stories of healing and compassion. Luke’s Gospel underscores Jesus’ ministry to the marginalized, the sick, the poor, and social outcasts, showing that the message of Christ is inclusive and caring.


Significance in Early Christianity
Luke's contributions are highly valued within Christian tradition because:

His firsthand experience with early Church leaders (particularly Paul) provides a unique perspective on the Christian mission in its formative years.
His detailed narrative helps bridge historical context with the spiritual message of salvation, making his writings a crucial resource for understanding the life and teachings of Jesus and the burgeoning community of believers.

Overall, Luke stands out as a key figure in early Christianity, providing not only a caring medical perspective but also a detailed historical account that continues to inspire modern readers with the inclusive nature of God’s salvation plan.

\v 11 Then an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right side of the altar of incense. \v 12 When Zechariah saw him, he was startled and was gripped with fear. \v 13 But the angel said to him: “Do not be afraid, Zechariah; your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to call him John. \v 14 He will be a joy and delight to you, and many will rejoice because of his birth, \v 15 for he will be great in the sight of the Lord. He is never to take wine or other fermented drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even before he is born. \v 16 He will bring back many of the people of Israel to the Lord their God. \v 17 And he will go on before the Lord, in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the parents to their children and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous—to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.”

\v 8 Once when Zechariah’s division was on duty and he was serving as priest before God, \v 9 he was chosen by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood, to go into the temple of the Lord and burn incense. \v 10 And when the time for the burning of incense came, all the assembled worshipers were praying outside.

\v 18 Zechariah asked the angel, “How can I be sure of this? I am an old man and my wife is well along in years.”

\v 19 The angel said to him, “I am Gabriel. I stand in the presence of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and to tell you this good news. \v 20 And now you will be silent and not able to speak until the day this happens, because you did not believe my words, which will come true at their appointed time.”
